- **Around 1750**: It existed. The position of the inscription 訓鍊院 on the original map was taken as the main building and the drill ground placed to its south.
- **Soldiers in training**: On the drill ground, 40 spear-bearing soldiers (5 columns by 8 rows) repeatedly thrust toward a flag-bearing instructor, and at the archery stand in front of the main building four archers aim at targets to the south. This follows the records that the Hullyeonwon administered the military examinations (including archery) and took part in the twice-monthly formation drills (seupjin); the number of people and their attire are estimates for display. ([Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, Hullyeonwon](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0065795))
- **Source**: [Seoul City, Seoul in My Hands, "Yi Sun-sin's military examination ground, the Hullyeonwon site"](https://mediahub.seoul.go.kr/archives/180498), [Korean Wikipedia, Hullyeonwon Park](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%ED%9B%88%EB%A0%A8%EC%9B%90%EA%B3%B5%EC%9B%90)

유명인 집터.body_en: Toggled with "House sites of notable figures" in the settings. Neither is drawn on the original map. The Song Si-yeol house site is shown as a walled tile-roofed house model; the Jeong Do-jeon house site, since there was no house there in 1750, is shown as a small marker stone. The models and their sizes are assumptions for display.

정도전 집터.body_en:
Said to be the site where Jeong Do-jeon, a founding merit subject of Joseon, lived. It is the area of today's Jongno-gu Office.

- **Period of existence**: After Jeong Do-jeon (1342–1398) was killed in the First Strife of the Princes in 1398, the house did not survive. The year the house was built is unconfirmed.
- **Around 1750**: **There was no house.** The Saboksi (太僕寺, Bureau of Royal Stables) stood in this area. For that reason only a small marker stone commemorating the old site is placed, instead of a walled tile-roofed house model.
- **Basis for location**: Exactly the point obtained by converting a what3words address supplied by a user into latitude and longitude (where the marker stone was first placed).
- **Source**: [Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, Jeong Do-jeon](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0050380), [Korean Wikipedia, Saboksi](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%82%AC%EB%B3%B5%EC%8B%9C)

송시열 집터.body_en:
The Seoul house site where Uam Song Si-yeol lived, a Seoul Tangible Cultural Heritage. A rock carved with the inscription "Jeungjubyeongnip" (曾朱壁立) and a stele reading "Uamgugi" (尤菴舊基, old site of Uam) survive.

- **Period of existence**: The 17th century, when Song Si-yeol (1607–1689) lived there. The house buildings do not survive.
- **Around 1750**: **It did not exist as Song Si-yeol's house.** It is a marker commemorating the old site.
- **Basis for location**: The designated address is Myeongnyun 1-ga, Jongno-gu, but on the original-map view it was placed at the midpoint of a line drawn northeast from Seonggyungwan to the city wall.
- **Source**: [Korea Heritage portal, Uam Song Si-yeol house site](https://www.heritage.go.kr/heri/cul/culSelectDetail.do?ccbaKdcd=21&ccbaAsno=0000570000000&ccbaCtcd=11), [Seoul City, "Reading Song Si-yeol in rock inscriptions across Seoul"](https://mediahub.seoul.go.kr/archives/2004185)

1750년과 맞지 않는 표시.body_en:
| Feature | Discrepancy |
| --- | --- |
| Gwanghwamun | In 1750 it was a ruin without a gate pavilion |
| Gyeongmogung | Built in 1764 |
| Jeong Do-jeon and Song Si-yeol house sites | Neither man's house existed in 1750. The Jeong Do-jeon site is shown only as a marker stone |
| Yukjo Street offices | The layout follows circa-1863 material |

후속 조사로 추가한 추정 위치 시설.title_en: Estimated-Location Features Added by Follow-up Research
후속 조사로 추가한 추정 위치 시설.body_en: Added following the research of 2026-09-16 and a user's request to display estimated locations. They are not treated as inscription-reading points on the original map or as measured reconstructions. The history of each institution or facility and the dating of its building form are managed separately.

군기시.body_en:
An office under the Ministry of War (Byeongjo) that made weapons, flags and other military equipment. In the later period it shared its role with the military commands' own production.

- **Period of existence**: Renamed from Gungigam to Gungisi in 1466. Abolished in 1884. This is the institution's history; the lifespan of individual office buildings is a separate matter.
- **Around 1750**: It existed. The excavated area on the Seoul City Hall site was georeferenced by estimate to north of Sungnyemun on the original map. It is not a reconstruction of the 1750 plan of the building remains.
- **Basis for location**: Placed in the area northwest of Nambyeolgung based on the positional relationship of the Gungisi remains on the City Hall site. It is not a point read from an inscription on the original map.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Gungisi](https://dh.aks.ac.kr/sillokwiki/index.php/%EA%B5%B0%EA%B8%B0%EC%8B%9C%28%E8%BB%8D%E5%99%A8%E5%AF%BA%29), [Introduction to the Gungisi Remains Exhibition Hall](https://museum.seoul.go.kr/www/intro/annexIntro/annex_gun/annex_gun_02.jsp?sso=ok)

영화당.body_en:
A hall in the rear garden of Changdeokgung from which state examinations and events on the Chundangdae grounds were directed.

- **Period of existence**: Year of construction unknown. Records of an order for repairs and their completion in 1692. It existed before the repairs.
- **Around 1750**: It existed. Estimated location in the Chundangdae area behind Changdeokgung. A five-bay hall was used as reference, but the dimensions and the extent of the event grounds are approximate.
- **Basis for location**: Estimated placement based on the documented relationship of lying in the rear-garden area north of the main hall of Changdeokgung and east of Buyongji pond. The precise plan is undetermined.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Yeonghwadang](https://dh.aks.ac.kr/sillokwiki/index.php/%EC%98%81%ED%99%94%EB%8B%B9%28%E6%9A%8E%E8%8A%B1%E5%A0%82%29), [Annals of Sukjong, 16th day of the 4th lunar month of 1692, repair of Yeonghwadang](https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/ksa_11804016_001), [Annals of Sukjong, 12th day of the 5th lunar month of 1692, completion of Yeonghwadang](https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/ksa_11805012_002)

청의정.body_en:
A thatched pavilion in the Ongnyucheon area of Changdeokgung. It is described as a space for reflecting on the meaning of farming, together with a small rice paddy.

- **Period of existence**: Record of construction in 1636. This does not mean that the surviving members and the present form of the paddy are all the same as at the time.
- **Around 1750**: There is evidence for its existence. Placed by estimate in the Ongnyucheon area. The thatched roof and the paddy are abstracted representations, and the cultivated area in 1750 is undetermined.
- **Basis for location**: Estimated location in the Ongnyucheon area north of the East Palace. Not a measured reconstruction of the paddy and waterways.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Chronology of the palaces](https://royal.cha.go.kr/ROYAL/contents/R311020000.do), [Cheonguijeong of Changdeokgung, a thatched pavilion built to consider the lives of farmers](https://ncms.nculture.org/pavilion/story/2377)

문헌각.body_en:
A building at Gyeongdeokgung where books were kept. Sukjong's inscription describes the storage of books in the library hall beside Gyeonghyeondang.

- **Period of existence**: Described as built in 1700. The date of demolition and the changes to the individual building are undetermined.
- **Around 1750**: It is taken to have continued as the library of Gyeongdeokgung. Only its relationship of being beside Gyeonghyeondang was confirmed, and it was placed by estimate within the palace grounds.
- **Basis for location**: Estimated location of a library placed in the eastern part of the Gyeongdeokgung grounds. The exact lots and distance between Gyeonghyeondang and Munheongak were not confirmed.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Munheongak](https://dh.aks.ac.kr/sillokwiki/index.php/%EB%AC%B8%ED%97%8C%EA%B0%81%28%E6%96%87%E7%8D%BB%E9%96%A3%29), [National Palace Museum of Korea, translation of Gunggwolji, inscription on Munheongak](https://www.gogung.go.kr/ebook/access/ecatalogt.jsp?Dir=219&callmode=admin&catimage=&eclang=ko&start=212&um=s)

애련정.body_en:
A pavilion in the rear garden of Changdeokgung, named by Sukjong in contemplation of the virtues of the lotus.

- **Period of existence**: Built in 1692. The recorded position in the middle of the pond differs from the present position at the pond's edge, and the date of the move is undetermined.
- **Around 1750**: It existed. The pavilion and pond were placed schematically in the rear-garden area. The pavilion's exact position in 1750 and the shape of the pond are estimates.
- **Basis for location**: Estimated location in the Aeryeonji pond area of the Changdeokgung rear garden. The model's placement at the pond's edge is an assumption for explanation, not a confirmed form for 1750.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Plaques and Couplets of the Palaces: Aeryeonjeong](https://m.cha.go.kr/newsBbz/selectNewsBbzView.do?edate=&mn=&newsItemId=155693299&pageIndex=10&sdate=&sectionId=ocp&strValue=&strWhere=)

취운정.body_en:
A small pavilion of the East Palace. It was built earlier than the neighboring Nakseonjae of today.

- **Period of existence**: Record of construction in 1686. Nakseonjae dates from 1847, a separate date.
- **Around 1750**: It existed. Placed by estimate in the hilly area between the southeast of Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung. The later Nakseonjae buildings are not included.
- **Basis for location**: Placed in the hilly area at the boundary of the East Palace. The coordinates of the surviving pavilion were not precisely verified against the original map.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Page recording the construction of Chwiunjeong and poems on it](https://www.gogung.go.kr/ebook/access/ecatalogt.jsp?Dir=219&callmode=admin&catimage=&eclang=ko&start=56&um=s), [Commentary on the dating of Changdeokgung buildings](https://contents.history.go.kr/mobile/km/view.do?levelId=km_039_0070_0040_0020)

청풍계 태고정.title_en: Taegojeong (Pavilion of High Antiquity) at Cheongpunggye
청풍계 태고정.body_en:
A thatched pavilion at the house of Kim Sang-yong in Cheongpunggye. Records survive of literati gatherings and of a visit by a later king.

- **Period of existence**: Described as built in 1607, with records of a gathering in 1620 and a visit in 1790. Its survival in 1750 is an estimate based on material from before and after.
- **Around 1750**: It is presumed to have still existed in 1750. Placed in the Cheongun-dong and Cheongpunggye area; the exact lot of the old house site is undetermined.
- **Basis for location**: Estimated location in the Cheongpunggye area east of Inwangsan and northwest of Gyeongbokgung. Not a point read from the coordinates of the "Baeksecheongpung" rock inscription itself or from the pavilion's foundation stones.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Taegojeong](https://dh.aks.ac.kr/sillokwiki/index.php/%ED%83%9C%EA%B3%A0%EC%A0%95%28%E5%A4%AA%E5%8F%A4%E4%BA%AD%29), [History Net, Taegojeong at Cheongpunggye and the spring gatherings](https://contents.history.go.kr/mobile/km/view.do?levelId=km_019_0040_0020_0030), [Annals of Jeongjo, 28th day of the 2nd lunar month of 1790, visit to Taegojeong](https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/kva_11402028_002), [Seoul City, Cheongpunggye and the Baeksecheongpung inscription in Cheongun-dong](https://mediahub.seoul.go.kr/archives/2007584)

남산 국사당.body_en:
A place of worship originally located on Namsan. It is distinguished from the present Guksadang, which was moved to Inwangsan around 1925.

- **Period of existence**: Located on Namsan during the Joseon period. The exact year of founding and the building's appearance in 1750 are undetermined. Moved to Inwangsan around 1925.
- **Around 1750**: Shown by estimate as a place of worship on Namsan. The present Inwangsan address and the arrangement of shamanic paintings were not projected back.
- **Basis for location**: Placed by estimate in the summit area of Namsan on the original map. It differs from the location of the surviving Guksadang on Inwangsan. The dimensions of the walls and buildings at the time are undetermined.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Guksadang on Inwangsan](https://digital.khs.go.kr/heri/heriDetail.do?ctptNo=1481100280000&ctptUid=13898859685433301677), [Historical changes and functions of the Seoul Guksadang](https://www.dbpia.co.kr/journal/articleDetail?nodeId=NODE08734618)

도화서.body_en:
The office concerned with state painting production and the training of court painters. It explains both the painters' profession and documentary paintings.

- **Period of existence**: An institution that continued through the Joseon period as Dohwawon and then Dohwaseo. The dates of the office's relocations and its lot in 1750 are subject to further review.
- **Around 1750**: The institution existed. Placed by estimate in the Gyeonpyeongbang area, without fixing it to a particular marker stone or the site of a modern building.
- **Basis for location**: Placed by estimate in the area north of Jongno, following the documentary record of Gyeonpyeongbang in the Central District. Because the office was relocated over time, there is uncertainty about its exact position.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Dohwaseo](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0015927), [A study of the Dohwaseo site](https://www.dbpia.co.kr/journal/articleDetail?nodeId=NODE10555498)

제용감.body_en:
The office in charge of the royal household's textiles and clothing, and of related work such as dyeing and weaving.

- **Period of existence**: Renamed Jeyonggam in 1409 and described as continuing until 1904. The institution's history and the locations of individual workshops are different matters.
- **Around 1750**: The institution existed. Placed by estimate in the Susong-dong and Sujinbang area. It is not asserted that every stage of dyeing and weaving took place within this lot.
- **Basis for location**: Area placement based on records of offices in the Susong-dong vicinity and the existing Sujinbang clue. The relocated marker stone was not used as the center point of the office.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Jeyonggam](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0051344), [Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, Jeyonggam and Dohwaseo in Jongno-gu](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0067017)

전생서.body_en:
An office south of Namsan that raised the livestock needed for state sacrifices and palace events.

- **Period of existence**: Renamed from Jeonguseo in 1460. Its organization is recorded in the Sokdaejeon (Supplement to the National Code) of Yeongjo's reign. Described as abolished in 1895.
- **Around 1750**: The institution existed. Shown by estimate in the Dunjibang and Huam-dong area south of Namsan, outside the city wall. The layout of the pens and the number of animals were not reproduced.
- **Basis for location**: Placed by estimate in the south of the original map, in the Dunjibang and Huam-dong area south of Namsan outside the city wall. No unconfirmed boundaries of the pens were drawn.
- **Model**: Estimated location, schematic model. Only the forms of pavilion, office hall and garden are abstracted; bay counts, dimensions and the extent of the walls require separate verification.
- **Source**: [Jeonsaengseo](https://dh.aks.ac.kr/sillokwiki/index.php/%EC%A0%84%EC%83%9D%EC%84%9C%28%E5%85%B8%E7%89%B2%E7%BD%B2%29), [Seoul City, Jeonsaengseo site in Huam-dong](https://mediahub.seoul.go.kr/archives/2013958)

1907년 궁궐.body_en: Separate records for the 1907 map. All models are simplified, with approximate placement and dimensions.

1907년 근정전.body_en:
Gyeongbokgung’s throne hall, rebuilt in 1867. A simplified five-by-five-bay hall with two roof tiers, a double terrace and courtyard. Placement and dimensions are approximate.

Rebuilt 1867 · conceptual model for 1907

1907년 중화전.body_en:
Junghwajeon, rebuilt in 1906. Approximate map placement and courtyard dimensions; a simplified 1-tier roof. No later interior alterations are depicted.

Rebuilt 1906 · conceptual model for 1907

1907년 인정전.body_en:
Injeongjeon, rebuilt in 1804. Approximate map placement and courtyard dimensions; a simplified 2-tier roof. No later interior alterations are depicted.
